hints: Focus on the rule for chirality, a chiral carbon must be attached to four completely different groups.
Look closely at the central carbon in citric acid, $\text{C(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$, and notice it has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups above and below it.
Now check the two middle carbons in isocitric acid one by one and confirm each one is bonded to four different groups.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for a chiral centre**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four single bonds to four different atoms or groups. If even two groups are the same, it cannot be chiral.

Rule to apply:
$$\text{chiral C = C bonded to 4 different groups}$$

**Check citric acid**

Citric acid is $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}-\text{C(OH)(CO}_2\text{H})-\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. The only possible centre is the middle carbon.

That middle carbon is bonded to: $\text{OH}$, $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups. Because two groups are the same, it is achiral. So citric acid has 0 chiral centres.

**Check isocitric acid**

Isocitric acid is $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}-\text{CH(CO}_2\text{H})-\text{CH(OH)(CO}_2\text{H})$. Look at the two middle carbons separately.

Middle carbon 1, $\text{CHCO}_2\text{H}$, is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and $\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$. All four are different, so it is chiral.

Middle carbon 2, $\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$, is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, and $\text{CH(CO}_2\text{H})\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$. All four are different, so it is also chiral. So isocitric acid has 2 chiral centres.

**Conclude the pair**

Citric acid has 0 and isocitric acid has 2. That matches the 0 and 2 row in the table.

options.A: Incorrect. Citric acid does not have 1 chiral centre because its central carbon has two identical CH2CO2H groups. Isocitric acid does not have only 1, both middle carbons are chiral.
options.B: Incorrect for citric acid. Students often assume the C(OH) carbon must be chiral because it has OH and CO2H, but they miss the two identical CH2CO2H arms which cancel chirality. The count of 2 for isocitric acid is correct.
options.C: Incorrect for isocitric acid. The 0 for citric acid is correct, but students choosing this often spot only one chiral carbon in isocitric acid and miss the second one.
options.D: Correct. Citric acid has 0 chiral centres due to the plane of symmetry through the central C with two identical CH2CO2H groups. Isocitric acid has 2 chiral centres, as both the CH(CO2H) carbon and the CH(OH)CO2H carbon each carry four different groups.
